title: Rule identifiability in elementary cellular automata under dynamical noise
description: Exact computation (no sampling, no seeds) of rule identifiability in elementary cellular automata under dynamical bit-flip noise. On a ring of 12 cells: zero-noise consistency classes for all 256 rules x 4096 initial states, the identifiability rate rho(f; eps) = lambda(eps) min_c nu_c(f; eps) for all 88 rule classes on a noise grid with the best noise level eps* per class, finite-horizon evidence margins from every initial state, and a boundary check with radius-2 generators. Version 0.2 adds the exact small-noise theory: the noise-selected cycles (minimum stochastic potential), the orders k_c and k* of the stationary neighbourhood frequencies and the asymptotics rho ~ a eps^k* log(1/eps), computed in integer arithmetic for all 88 classes at n = 12 and for ring sizes n = 4..20 (checked certificates for n = 12 and n <= 14). This settles the classes that version 0.1 left to a numerical trend and corrects class 106. Version 0.3 adds a study of the 13 classes whose small-noise order k* changes side with the ring size (report_ring_size.md): the mechanisms, computed for n <= 22 (in ten of the classes a spatially periodic crystal that exists only when its period divides n, or a zero state that cannot be left by one flip), and two statements proved for all n by the independent verification session: for rule 154, k* = 1 if and only if n is a power of two (n >= 3); for class 94, k* = 1 at every n >= 6 divisible by 3. These proofs are not peer reviewed. The note itself is unchanged (version 0.2). Includes code, data files with a SHA-256 manifest, the note as PDF, and the reports of the independent verification sessions.
notes: Definitions, code, computation, figures and text were produced by Claude (Anthropic) in sessions directed by the author on 4 and 15 October 2026 (version 0.1), on 8 and 9 November 2026 (version 0.2) and on 13 to 15 November 2026 (version 0.3). For each version an independent Claude session that had not seen the work recomputed samples from the definitions and checked the numbers against the data files (VERIFICATION.md, VERIFICATION_v02.md, VERIFICATION_ring_size.md). For version 0.3 that session also proved the two statements that hold for all n; its proofs were read a second time, with separate code, in a further Claude session.
